problem: Development speed was being lost after coding: parallel PR fan-out, stale merge-bases, silent workflow starts, broad blocking suites, false-positive regression oracles and passive queue waiting created delivery latency and conflict amplification.
root_cause: PRs were being used as the primary parallelism unit instead of isolated agent workspaces feeding a bounded integration lane.
Broad regression suites were in the blocking path even when the changed delta did not touch those risk surfaces.
Superseded runs, stale merge-bases and silent workflow starts were treated as waiting states instead of recoverable delivery incidents.
The system reacted after CI trouble instead of predicting conflict, queue pressure and likely failure surfaces before fan-out.
Gate selection was mostly static; unrelated broad assurance could still enter the blocking path.
Recovery logic existed as policy but lacked one explicit scheduled supervisor that continuously reconciled open PR heads.
fix: Use isolated parallel agent workspaces but one rolling integration candidate per conflict contract.
Expand safe TURBO scope to 24 files while keeping protected infrastructure/security/schema surfaces excluded.
Make BRAIN reuse the same TURBO risk classification instead of duplicating full suites for safe deltas.
Move unrelated broad assurance to an asynchronous post-merge main workflow.
Set explicit first-signal, turbo and standard latency SLOs and make breaches trigger same-lineage recovery.
Auto-cancel superseded runs and preserve tested candidates across non-overlapping main drift.
Add predictive admission using changed-path, contract, dependency and historical delivery signals.
Add adaptive gate planning: only relevant risk/dependency/contract/security/data/schema gates block; unrelated assurance runs in shadow.
Add a five-minute single-flight delivery supervisor that heals zero-run and stale-run heads on the same PR lineage.
Calibrate predictions daily against actual queue, conflict, gate, rollback and production-readback outcomes.
Make frontend/backend/QA/release/learning agents explicit roles under one coordinator and one production authority.
